name: Prasopita (Crispy Greek Leek and Feta Pie)

cookwares.name: rolling pin or thin wooden pastry dowel

ingredients.name: bread flour, plus more for dusting
room-temperature water, plus more as needed

instructions.primary_message: Pick the dill fronds from the stems and roughly chop them. Crumble the sheep’s-milk feta cheese.
instructions.secondary_message:
⅓ cup lightly packed fresh dill
7 oz sheep’s-milk feta cheese

instructions.primary_message: For the Phyllo Dough: In a large bowl, whisk together bread flour, whole wheat flour, and salt. Add vinegar, 3 tablespoons olive oil, and water, and mix by hand until a rough dough forms and no dry flour remains.

Transfer dough to a clean work surface and knead with the heel of your hand until smooth and supple, 2 to 3 minutes. Return dough to bowl and rub remaining 1 teaspoon oil evenly over its surface. Cover bowl with plastic wrap or clean kitchen towel and let rest at room temperature for 30 minutes or up to 1 hour. Alternatively, refrigerate dough in an airtight container for up to 24 hours; let stand at room temperature for about 2 hours before rolling.

For the Leek Filling: In a 12-inch skillet, heat oil over medium until shimmering. Add leeks by the handful, stirring and allowing each addition to wilt slightly before adding more. Add salt and cook, stirring occasionally and reducing heat if leeks begin to brown, until leeks are tender and translucent but retain their shape, 15 to 18 minutes. Transfer to a large bowl and let cool to room temperature.

For Assembling the Pie: Adjust oven rack to middle position and preheat oven to 400°F. Add dill and/or parsley, oregano, and feta to bowl with cooled leeks and gently fold until evenly combined. Set filling aside.

Transfer dough to a clean work surface and knead briefly to incorporate any oil remaining on its surface. Divide dough into 4 equal portions. Cup your hand around each portion and move it in a circular motion against the counter to form a smooth ball. Keep dough covered with plastic wrap or kitchen towel when not working with it to prevent it from drying out.

Lightly flour your work surface. Working with 1 dough ball at a time, use a rolling pin to roll dough into a roughly 5-inch round, rotating it a quarter turn after each pass to maintain an even shape. Lightly flour both sides, set aside, and repeat with remaining dough. Beginning with the first round, roll each portion into a roughly 6-inch round. Let rounds rest for 5 minutes.

Working with 1 round at a time, roll dough from the center outward, rotating it frequently, until it forms a thin, roughly 18- by 13-inch rectangle. To elongate dough, concentrate the rolling pin along 2 opposite sides. If needed, drape dough over the backs of your hands and gently stretch it from the center outward (see notes). Use flour sparingly to prevent sticking; too much will make dough more difficult to stretch. If dough tears, pinch it together to seal. The rectangle does not need to be perfect.

Brush an 18- by 13-inch rimmed baking sheet evenly with 1 tablespoon olive oil. Carefully lay first phyllo sheet in prepared baking sheet and brush evenly with 1 tablespoon oil. Roll and stretch a second portion of dough as directed in step 7 and place it over first sheet.

Spread leek filling evenly over phyllo, leaving a 1/2-inch border around the edges. Roll and stretch a third portion of dough as directed in step 7 and place it over filling. Brush evenly with 1 tablespoon oil. Roll and stretch final portion of dough and place it over third sheet.
Working around the perimeter of the pie, fold the overhanging bottom layers of phyllo up and over the top layers, then crimp the edges together to seal in the filling.

Brush top evenly with remaining 2 tablespoons olive oil. Dip your fingertips in water and flick water lightly and evenly over the surface. Sprinkle with sesame seeds, if using. Using a paring knife, score the top layers into 8 to 12 portions without cutting all the way through the pie.
Bake until phyllo is crisp and deep golden brown, 45 to 55 minutes.
Transfer baking sheet to a wire rack and let pie cool for at least 30 minutes. Transfer to a cutting board, cut along scored lines, and serve.

description: Learn how to make prasopita, a Greek savory pie filled with tender leeks, tangy feta, fresh herbs, and crispy homemade crust.
notes:
Total time, including resting: 3 hr 15 min.

Optional or for serving: 2 tablespoons sesame seeds, optional

Optional substitutions: apple cider vinegar → unseasoned rice vinegar

Notes: The whole wheat flour gives the phyllo a subtly nutty, toasted flavor. If unavailable, replace it with an equal weight of bread flour.
Leeks vary significantly in size. For the most consistent filling, rely on the listed weight and prepared volume rather than the number of leeks.
For the best flavor and texture, purchase feta in brine and crumble it yourself. Pre-crumbled feta tends to be drier and less flavorful. Greek feta made with sheep’s milk or a combination of sheep’s and goat’s milk is preferred.
If the dough repeatedly springs back while rolling, cover it and let it rest for 5 minutes before continuing. This brief rest lets the gluten relax, making the dough easier to stretch.

Make-ahead and storage: The phyllo dough can be prepared up to 24 hours in advance and refrigerated in an airtight container. Let it stand at room temperature for about 2 hours before rolling.
The leeks can be cooked up to 1 day in advance and refrigerated in an airtight container. Let them return to room temperature before mixing with the herbs and feta and assembling the pie.
Leftover prasopita can be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 5 days. For the crispest phyllo, reheat the pie uncovered in a 350°F oven until warmed through.
author: Sharon Brenner
